title: 'Loch Lomond' controversy in Britain
summary: In 1948 she went to the UK; the English resented the swing Loch Lomond more than the Scots.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yeah. In '48 when I went over, you know I was afforded this trip to "Loch Lomond"--the British Overseas Air Corporation sponsored my trip from London to Scotland. And I sang "Loch Lomond" on the shores of "Loch Lomond", wondering what the reaction was going to be. Because previously -- but the funny thing about it --

They did some reaction in England, yeah.
The British resented it more than the Scots!
Yeah, they still think it was the worst thing --
Some guy in Jersey brought me a xerox copy of the original controversy that appeared in the Melody Maker. It went on for years!

Yeah. And so they're still -- When I went over there, they did not ask me. When I did Loch Lomond at the London Casino the first time, there was not that much enthusiasm. They wanted to hear 'The Folks Who Lived On The Hill.'
